lede: The biggest thing on the calendar this week is the Carhenge redevelopment, which hits two separate bodies in one day — September 30 — when HARC reviews three preliminary large-scale building applications for 700 W. Pacific Ave and the Town Council simultaneously holds an appeal hearing on the lot subdivision that underlies the whole project. Elsewhere, the Gondola Leadership Committee faces a real fork in the road on September 28, choosing between federal funding with federal strings or local financing with local control. The County's work session on September 30 also takes up a proposed Employee Housing Impact Fee, which could have broad consequences for how growth gets paid for across San Miguel County.

notable.stake: Committee votes on federal vs. local financing model for the gondola project.
